title: AI Stocks Crash After Midterms: Is Wall Street Overreacting?
creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
summary: Jose Najarro argues the post-midterm crash in AI stocks is an overreaction. Neocloud names have been hit hard - Nebius down roughly 47-48% over five months, Oracle down about 18% in a month, CoreWeave down about 48% and Applied Digital down about 40% in a month - after fears that the election results, especially in Texas, will slow data-centre buildouts.  He says the market exaggerates: AI demand is not stopping, construction already under way will continue, and the Texas governor-elect wants partnership and community protections rather than ending data centres. His own move is to sell some lower-beta Mag 7 holdings and rotate into high-beta AI names in tranches. He is most positive on IREN after its earnings: management lowered capex and refused to chase growth at any cost, while pricing looks very strong - long-term contracts at $22 million per megawatt over five years with 90% of GPU capex prepaid, short-term contracts up to $40 million per megawatt, and H100s recontracted at double the old price. He reads supply-chain players slowing 2027 capacity expansion as cycle-extending, not a demand problem. No explicit buy, hold or sell call is made on any single ticker besides his reiterated bullishness on IREN and the neocloud space. Caption garbles: 'Nebulas/Nebas/Nebulius' for Nebius, 'Kio' for CoreWeave, 'Mac 7s/MAX7s' for Mag 7, and the Texas governor-elect's name is garbled.

calls.thesis: Reiterated bullish: still very much bullish on the neocloud space and rotating Mag 7 proceeds into high-beta AI names in tranches. IREN's earnings showed disciplined capex (lowered, not chasing growth at any cost) and a strong pricing bull case: long-term contracts $22M per megawatt over 5 years with 90% of GPU capex prepaid, short-term contracts up to $40M/MW, and H100s recontracted at double the old price.
calls.price_at_call: No price stated; neoclouds sharply down (Nebius ~48% in 5 months)
